messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
In our own Solar System, **Jupiter** is the largest planet—about 1 300 times more massive than Earth and roughly 11 times its diameter.

When astronomers look beyond the Solar System, they find planets even bigger. One of the most impressive examples is **HD 100546 b**, an exoplanet orbiting the young star HD 100546 (about 320 light‑years away). It has a radius estimated at around **20–25 Earth radii** (roughly twice Jupiter’s size) and a mass of about **10–15 times Jupiter’s mass**. That makes it one of the largest confirmed exoplanets discovered so far.

There may well be even larger “super‑Jupiters” out there—some estimates suggest planets with masses up to ~30–40 Jupiter masses—but many of those candidates sit near the boundary between giant planets and brown dwarfs, making classification tricky. For now, HD 100546 b remains among the biggest planetary bodies we’ve confidently identified.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What is the largest planet in the universe?" We need to answer. According to known data, the largest confirmed exoplanet is HD 100546 b or something like that. But we can provide general info: Jupiter is the largest in our solar system; but there are larger exoplanets like HD 100546 b (~20 Earth radii). Provide context. No tool call needed.
